Consider the region bounded by the curve $x=-\sqrt{y}+y$ and the $y$-axis from $y=0$ to $y=1$ (shown in the picture). Using the shell method, calculate the volume of the solid generated when that region is rotated about the $x$-axis.

$V=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The region is enclosed between the $y$-axis, the curve $x=-\sqrt{y}+y$, and the lines $y=0$ and $y=1.$ So, we need to integrate from $y=0$ to $y=1.$ 

Since the region lies to the left of the $y$-axis, the width of the cylindrical shells is given by $f(y)=0-(-\sqrt{y}+y)=\sqrt{y}-y.$ Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{c}^{d}yf(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}y(\sqrt{y}-y)\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({y}^{3/2}-{y}^{2})\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi ({\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{3/2}\,\text{d}y-{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y) \\  & =2\pi ({\frac{2{y}^{5/2}}{5}|}_{0}^{1}-{\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}|}_{0}^{1}) \\  & =2\pi ((\frac{2}{5}-0)-(\frac{1}{3}-0)) \\  & =2\pi (\frac{2}{5}-\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =\frac{2\pi }{15}\end{aligned}
$$
